slides.title: Is your frame build costing you speed?
slides.sub: Get bearings, spacers and axles right first time

slides.title: Count your parts first
slides.body: A pair of four wheel skates needs eight wheels and sixteen bearings. A triskate pair needs six wheels and twelve bearings.

slides.title: Why every wheel needs a spacer
slides.caption: The spacer between the two bearings takes the clamping load from the axle.

slides.title: Seat bearings straight
slides.body: Press each bearing in squarely with your thumbs until it sits flush. If it goes in stiffly, check it is not tilted before you push.

slides.title: One drop of oil, before the build
slides.body: Add one drop per bearing and spin it by hand to spread the oil. A flooded bearing collects dust and drags.

slides.title: Axles: firm, then stop
slides.body: Tightening past firm only loads the bearings. Spin the wheel after. It should turn freely and quietly for several seconds.

slides.title: Measure your boot mounting
slides.body: Measure from the centre of the front slot to the centre of the rear slot. Edge to edge reads long and points you at the wrong standard.
